hypotheses.claim: TEOA, more than TEA, may participate non-innocently in substrate-associated chemistry by forming amine- or catalyst-linked CO2 adducts or stabilizing intermediates, thereby changing apparent selectivity without requiring a different primary quenching step. A discriminating prediction is that donor substitution changes substrate- or intermediate-associated spectroscopic signatures or CO2-origin-bounded behavior even when electron-supply observables are similar.
hypotheses.alternative: No donor-specific substrate adduct or intermediate stabilization is important, and any TEA/TEOA selectivity difference is fully explained by quenching kinetics, cobalt-state changes, or uncontrolled background reactions.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: P01 is adequate because it keeps the Co-bpy context while allowing donor substitution under one baseline; the key comparison is TEA versus TEOA with matched CO2 atmosphere and medium. Supplementary transfer to P02 is lower value here because homogeneous donor-side quenching there does not directly test substrate-associated adduct chemistry.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Direct observation of such intermediates in a TEA/TEOA Co-bpy comparison is absent from the supplied data, so this is a falsifiable transfer hypothesis rather than an established mechanism. Some related claims are author interpretations and may not generalize across metals or solvents.

candidates.title: CO2-associated speciation versus donor identity before illumination
candidates.purpose: Test whether matched P01 mixtures containing TEA or TEOA show different pre-illumination CO2-associated solution signatures, and whether any donor-dependent signal requires cobalt/bipyridine presence. This addresses the H05 prediction of donor-linked substrate or intermediate association without presuming catalytic relevance.
candidates.source_to_proposal: Sources report or interpret TEOA as capable of CO2 trapping or catalyst-adduct chemistry in non-cobalt systems and show that medium can alter observable intermediates; this proposal transfers only the testable prediction that donor identity may change observable CO2-associated states under matched Co-bpy conditions. Operando/isotopic assignment evidence is used only to justify control logic, not to assume identical species in P01.

comparisons.inference: If CO2-dependent spectra differ reproducibly between TEA and TEOA under otherwise matched conditions, that supports donor-associated speciation differences; it does not by itself identify whether signals are bulk amine-CO2 species or catalyst-linked adducts.
CO2-dependent features present only with CO2 bound the assignment to substrate-associated chemistry rather than donor or catalyst background in TEA medium.
CO2-dependent features present only with CO2 bound the assignment to substrate-associated chemistry rather than donor or catalyst background in TEOA medium.

If a feature appears with TEOA but not no-amine under CO2, the donor is associated with the species population; however cobalt, bpy, and g-C3N4 remain present, so the signal may still be bulk medium speciation rather than catalyst-linked.

procedure: Prepare matched P01 mixtures using the literature-supported component set and fixed solvent composition, varying only donor identity as assigned; verify exact baseline formulation from supplied system evidence before execution.
Equilibrate each group with the assigned gas in the dark for a matched period determined by a pilot that confirms stable spectra over repeated short acquisitions.

Acquire paired solution-focused IR and/or NMR spectra with corresponding solvent/background references; if feasible, also collect spectra after removing suspended solids or with solid-free reference aliquots to separate bulk-solution from suspension contributions.

Use difference analysis between CO2 and inert counterparts and compare TEA, TEOA, and no-amine groups; only advance tentative assignments that are reproducible across replicate preparations and instrument backgrounds.
measurements: IR spectra of pre-illumination mixtures, emphasizing donor- and CO2-dependent new bands or band shifts relative to inert controls
NMR spectra of pre-illumination mixtures, emphasizing donor- and CO2-dependent new resonances, broadening, or chemical-shift changes
Difference spectra between CO2 and inert conditions for each donor condition
Replicate-to-replicate reproducibility of the above signatures under independently prepared matched samples

If phase-separated or clarified aliquots are feasible, comparison of bulk-solution versus suspension-containing signal contributions; this cannot by itself establish catalytic on-pathway relevance or exact structure
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be reproducible CO2-dependent signatures that differ between TEA and TEOA under otherwise matched P01 conditions, especially if TEOA shows additional or stronger features absent in inert controls and not reproduced by the no-amine CO2 sample. Stronger support would come from consistent assignment logic across two observables, such as IR plus NMR, while still remaining descriptive rather than mechanistic proof.
candidates.refutes: H05 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in any CO2-dependent pre-illumination signature under matched conditions, or if all apparent donor differences disappear after background subtraction, replicate preparation, and gas-control checks. It is also weakened if observed features are equally present under inert gas, indicating donor/background rather than CO2-associated origin.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if signals are too weak, unresolved, or irreproducible; if TEA and TEOA differ but only alongside uncontrolled pH, water-content, or solubility changes; or if spectra show donor-dependent bulk amine-CO2 speciation but cannot separate that from catalyst-associated adducts. A null result does not exclude transient light-induced differences.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations or acquisition settings. Use the verified P01 baseline composition from supplied evidence. Run a short pilot to set gas-equilibration time, sample concentration window, and spectral averaging so that major solvent and donor backgrounds are stable and not detector-saturating. If both IR and NMR are attempted, choose the method giving reproducible CO2-minus-inert difference signals first; add the second method only if it offers independent assignment value. If signal overlap prevents interpretation, prioritize isotopic or background controls only after basic detectability is confirmed.
candidates.limitations: This experiment is characterization only and cannot establish that any detected species lies on the catalytic pathway or controls CO/H2 selectivity. TEA/TEOA change multiple chemical properties beyond simple donor strength, so donor identity is a bundled factor even in the single-factor contrast. Because cobalt, bpy, and g-C3N4 remain present in all main groups, any observed signal may arise from bulk amine-CO2 chemistry, catalyst-linked adducts, support-associated species, or combinations thereof. Pre-illumination measurements may miss the operating photochemical state.

candidates.title: Operando isotope-sensitive IR for TEA versus TEOA
candidates.purpose: Test whether donor identity changes reaction-state IR features consistent with CO2-associated or hydrogen-involving species in the P01 Co-bpy context, using symmetric isotope and negative controls so any TEA-versus-TEOA difference is bounded in both donor conditions rather than inferred from products alone.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV080 and GX008 support operando IR with isotope and negative controls as a transferable strategy. EV031 and EV029 motivate the narrower proposal that donor identity can alter intermediate populations or CO2-associated adduct chemistry, but they do not establish the same species in Co-bpy. This revised card therefore compares TEA and TEOA under matched conditions and applies parallel assignment controls on both donor sides where feasible.

procedure: Verify an IR-compatible reaction cell and establish stable pre-illumination baselines for the complete P01 medium with TEA and with TEOA, using the same optical path and gas handling across all groups.
Run matched illuminated operando or near-operando CO2 experiments for TEA and TEOA, including corresponding cobalt-absent references, with identical acquisition timing and reactor configuration.

After donor-comparison reproducibility is confirmed, repeat each donor condition with 13CO2 and, where spectral quality and formulation stability remain acceptable, with D2O substitution of the aqueous component.
Process spectra against pre-illumination and component-matched references, then compare donor-dependent band emergence, isotope shifts, persistence, and decay across the paired TEA and TEOA datasets.

Relate any donor-dependent spectral differences to separately measured matched catalytic outputs only descriptively, avoiding unique structural or pathway claims unless isotope and control behavior are internally consistent on both donor sides.
measurements: Time-resolved IR spectra under illumination for all groups.
Wavenumber positions, isotope shifts, and temporal evolution of donor-dependent bands under TEA and TEOA.
Presence or absence of candidate bands in cobalt-present versus cobalt-absent references for each donor.
Symmetry of 13CO2 and D2O assignment behavior across TEA and TEOA conditions.
Signal-to-noise, baseline stability, repeatability across replicate runs, and degree of band overlap.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in reaction-state IR features under otherwise matched conditions, with at least one donor-dependent feature showing internally consistent isotope behavior and cobalt dependence on the relevant donor side. The strongest support is when analogous assignment controls bound TEA and TEOA features differently, consistent with donor-specific CO2-associated or hydrogen-involving chemistry rather than simple background differences.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible donor-dependent reaction-state IR differences beyond baseline noise or generic medium changes, or that apparent differences disappear once symmetric isotope and cobalt-absent controls are applied. That outcome would favor explanations centered elsewhere, such as quenching kinetics, cobalt-state changes not resolved here, or uncontrolled catalytic variability.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are dominated by overlap, weak signals, or baseline drift; if D2O or 13CO2 causes broad perturbation without interpretable assignment value; if only one donor condition yields usable isotope-control data; or if donor-dependent bands cannot be separated from cobalt-free backgrounds. In that case the experiment remains descriptive and cannot cleanly discriminate H05 from competing explanations.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature conditions. Use the source-verified P01 formulation where available; otherwise first pilot each donor condition separately to find the highest concentration, path length, and collection time that preserve unsaturated absorbance and stable baselines. Keep reactor geometry, illumination, gas handling, and acquisition timing identical across TEA and TEOA. Apply 13CO2 and D2O only after the corresponding unlabeled donor condition gives reproducible transient bands. If D2O destabilizes one donor formulation or causes severe rate collapse, retain that arm as a bounded assignment aid and narrow inference accordingly rather than treating TEA and TEOA as fully matched.
candidates.limitations: Evidence is transferred from non-Co systems and general methods. Band assignment may remain ambiguous because donor, solvent, bicarbonate or carbonate, products, and cobalt-ligand features can overlap. Isotope substitution can alter kinetics as well as frequencies. Near-operando spectra may miss the true operating state, and operando IR alone cannot prove the primary quenching route, exact adduct identity, or whether a detected species is on-path rather than spectator. Cobalt-absent controls bound background contributions but do not separately isolate all non-cobalt components.

candidates.title: 13CO2-bounded TEA versus TEOA benchmark with matched background controls
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA/TEOA difference in apparent CO/H2 selectivity remains when counted CO is explicitly confirmed as CO2-derived within the P01 Co-bpy comparison, while checking donor-dependent background gas formation under no-CO2 and dark conditions.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV021 motivates explicit isotope origin-bounding because CO was reported from CO2 rather than TEOA decomposition in a different TEOA-containing photochemical system. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and altered active species can confound product assignment. GX008 supports negative controls and reproducible 13CO2 labeling in photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. EV063 shows that in a CoCl2/bpy-containing photocatalytic system, CO and H2 outputs are medium-sensitive, so the TEA/TEOA comparison should keep all non-donor factors matched. Proposed transfer: apply isotope-bounded product analysis to the matched P01 donor substitution; this bounds carbon-origin alternatives but does not directly identify adducts or operating cobalt states.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-factor test: if electron-supply observables are otherwise matched in the broader program, a donor-dependent change in 13CO formation or 13CO/H2 ratio is consistent with donor-linked substrate or intermediate effects but is not uniquely mechanistic.
Tests whether CO detected with TEOA requires supplied CO2; residual unlabeled or non-CO2-derived CO would limit selectivity interpretation.
Parallel CO2-origin check for the TEA case; donor-specific background gas formation would confound the head-to-head comparison if substantial.

Multi-factor descriptive control only because two factors differ if one donor is selected; it checks need for illumination but cannot isolate a donor effect and should not be read as a causal donor contrast.

procedure: Verify or pilot-match the P01 baseline composition, reactor geometry, gas-handling sequence, and analytical workflow, then prepare one TEOA and one TEA formulation differing only in donor identity.
Run illuminated reactions under 13CO2 for G01 and G02 with matched timing and sampling; in parallel or separate matched runs perform inert-gas controls G03 and G04 and one dark control G05.
Analyze headspace for CO isotopologues and H2 in the same workflow, using standards/blanks needed to separate labeled CO from background and to check carryover.
Compare donor-dependent CO, H2, and isotopic fractions only within runs that pass control checks for low dark production and low inert-gas CO background.
measurements: Headspace CO isotopologue signals distinguishing 13CO from unlabeled/background CO
Total CO amount together with isotopic fraction assigned as CO2-derived
H2 amount measured in the same samples
CO/H2 ratio and 13CO/H2 ratio under matched conditions
Dark-control and inert-gas-control gas outputs as background bounds
Replicate-to-replicate consistency of gas analysis and isotopic assignment
candidates.supports: Support for H05 is stronger if G01 and G02 show a reproducible donor-dependent difference in the CO2-derived 13CO fraction or 13CO/H2 ratio while inert-gas controls remain low for donor-derived background CO and the broader program finds no commensurate donor difference in upstream electron-supply observables. This would show that the TEA/TEOA effect is not merely an artifact of counting non-CO2 carbon as product, though it would still not prove adduct identity.
candidates.refutes: H05 is weakened if the apparent TEA/TEOA CO difference disappears once analysis is restricted to confirmed 13CO2-derived CO, or if donor-dependent CO appears similarly in inert-gas or dark controls, indicating that background chemistry can account for the prior selectivity difference. H05 is also weakened if 13CO/H2 remains indistinguishable between donors under well-matched conditions and controls.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if isotopic resolution is insufficient, baseline CO contamination or carryover is non-negligible, medium matching between TEA and TEOA is not credible, or any observed donor effect is comparable to run-to-run variability. A retained donor difference in 13CO origin confirms a real product-origin effect but still cannot distinguish adduct stabilization from cobalt-state or quenching explanations.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, light dose, or runtime. Use the verified P01 baseline if explicitly available; otherwise run a pilot to choose a reaction duration that gives quantifiable CO and H2 above blank yet remains before obvious saturation or severe deactivation. Calibrate gas analysis with labeled and unlabeled CO standards or equivalent instrument checks, confirm no memory effect by blank injections, and use the same sampling cadence and reactor volume across all groups. If TEA substitution changes pH, conductivity, or phase behavior enough to break comparability, document this and either predefine a matched-medium adjustment pilot or treat the comparison as partially confounded rather than a strict single-factor test.
candidates.limitations: This candidate bounds carbon origin but does not directly observe amine-CO2 adducts, catalyst-linked intermediates, or operating cobalt speciation. TEA and TEOA can change multiple hidden properties even when nominal formulation is matched, including proton activity and solvation, so a donor effect here is not uniquely attributable to adduct stabilization. The dark control is intentionally limited and, if only one donor is used, becomes a multi-factor descriptive check rather than a donor-specific contrast. Transfer from the cited literature is methodological and cautionary, not direct proof for P01.

candidates.title: TEA/TEOA matched catalytic readout with built-in negative controls and optional isotope follow-up
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution persists after stricter matching and core negative controls, while narrowing the claim to a bounded comparison unless a validated adduct-sensitive signal is first established.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV011 supports the competing explanation that both TEA and TEOA can act through reductive quenching and donor-radical formation. EV029 and GX011 provide transferable but non-Co evidence that TEOA can participate in catalyst/CO2-associated adduct chemistry beyond simple donation. GX008 supports adding negative controls and 13CO2 checks in homogeneous photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. Proposed transfer: in the stated Co-bpy comparison platform, first confirm whether a TEA/TEOA catalytic difference is reproducible under tightly matched conditions and core controls, then only integrate any adduct-sensitive observable if a pilot shows that the method is detectable and comparable in this platform. This is a proposal, not a reported Co-bpy result.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-factor comparison for reproducibility of TEA versus TEOA effects on CO/H2 and on any pilot-qualified observables. If quenching observables are similar within pre-set repeatability bounds yet catalytic outputs differ, H05 remains viable but not proven; if both catalytic and quenching observables are similar, the reported donor difference weakens.
Necessity control for cobalt-dependent catalysis or cobalt-linked signal assignment under the TEOA condition; it does not isolate donor effects.
Necessity control for light-driven behavior under the TEOA condition; it helps bound background product formation or donor decomposition.
Origin-bounded follow-up for the TEOA condition if products are detectable; useful for excluding obvious non-CO2 product-origin artifacts but not sufficient to prove a specific adduct mechanism.

procedure: Prepare matched TEA and TEOA formulations by changing only donor identity, and verify identical reactor geometry, gas handling, illumination setup, sampling schedule, and product-analysis workflow before catalysis.
Run the two catalytic groups together with no-cobalt and dark controls; measure CO and H2 for all groups and acquire the same quenching readout for TEA and TEOA with identical references and blanks.

Only if a pilot demonstrates a detectable, reproducible adduct-sensitive or intermediate-sensitive signal in this platform, collect that signal for both donors under the same sample state and timing window.

If catalytic products exceed the laboratory detection threshold with acceptable repeatability, repeat the two catalytic groups under 13CO2 as an origin-bounded follow-up using the same analytical workflow.
measurements: CO and H2 quantified together by one unchanged analytical method across all groups
Predefined quenching observable for the platform, such as emission quenching or excited-state decay of the light-absorbing component
If pilot-qualified, one adduct-sensitive or intermediate-sensitive spectral feature collected with matched blanks and backgrounds
For optional 13CO2 groups, isotopic product assignment if detectable
Covariates affecting comparability, including pH or apparent basicity proxy, optical density, visible precipitation, and color change
Replicate-to-replicate variability and practical detection limits for each readout
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution under the matched catalytic comparison that remains after cobalt and dark controls validate the assay, together with similar quenching observables within a pre-specified repeatability window and, if available, a donor-dependent adduct-sensitive or intermediate-sensitive signal. Consistent 13CO2 product origin would strengthen interpretation but would still not by itself establish a specific adduct structure.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that the TEA/TEOA catalytic difference disappears under stricter matching, or that any remaining catalytic difference is accompanied by clearly different quenching behavior large enough to account for it, or that the observed products/signals are reproduced in no-cobalt or dark controls in ways that undermine a cobalt-linked donor-specific interpretation.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if quenching and downstream-sensitive observables both change together, if the adduct-sensitive method cannot be qualified in this platform, if products are near detection limits, if isotope follow-up is below sensitivity, or if donor substitution changes bulk medium properties enough that multiple latent factors vary despite nominal matching.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations or irradiation settings. Use the researcher-stated Co-bpy baseline values only if explicitly verified in the supplied material; otherwise perform a pilot to set a workable window where both donors give measurable but not overloaded product signals and where the chosen quenching assay is above background. Define in advance what counts as 'similar quenching' using the assay repeatability from replicate baseline measurements, not a literature threshold. Add the adduct-sensitive module only if the pilot shows a reproducible signal in both donors with the same references and no uncontrolled precipitation.
candidates.limitations: This revision narrows the claim from a strong mechanistic discriminator to a staged comparison with controls because the supplied record does not establish a validated adduct-sensitive method in the target platform. TEA and TEOA can change several medium properties beyond donor identity, so even the primary contrast may combine donor, base, proton-management, and solvation effects. Negative controls improve assignment but do not identify the exact active intermediate. 13CO2 constrains origin claims but does not prove a productive donor-catalyst adduct.

candidates.title: Amine omission and TEA versus TEOA contrast under matched CO2 exposure
candidates.purpose: Test whether donor presence is necessary for any CO2-associated spectroscopic signature and whether TEOA gives a donor-identity-specific signature or product-origin pattern beyond a generic amine effect in the P01 Co-bpy context.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV029 and GX011 motivate a transferable hypothesis that TEOA can participate in CO2- or catalyst-linked adduct chemistry rather than acting only as an electron donor. EV061 adds the alternative that amine effects may instead reflect quenching and CO2-solvation behavior. GX008 supports matched negative controls and 13CO2 origin checks. Proposed transfer is limited: these sources are not direct TEA-versus-TEOA evidence in the target Co-bpy system, so the experiment is framed as a discrimination test, not mechanism confirmation.

comparisons.inference: Omission tests whether any amine-linked operando signature or catalytic response requires donor/additive presence at all; it does not test TEOA specificity.
Substitution tests donor identity specificity under a nominally matched baseline. A TEOA-only signature or origin-bounded behavior would support H05 more than a generic amine effect.
Distinguishes a generic TEA amine effect from no-amine background, helping bound whether TEA can reproduce any amine-associated state without implying equivalence to TEOA.
Isotopic substitution can test whether detected gaseous carbon products or selected vibrational features track CO2 origin; it cannot by itself identify the full intermediate structure.

procedure: Prepare the four matched P01 group formulations from the same component stocks and reactor setup, changing only the listed factor values and documenting pH or other medium covariates rather than assuming equality.

Expose each group to the assigned CO2 isotopic atmosphere, collect pre-illumination and illuminated operando or near-operando spectra using the same background and reference protocol, and run catalytic sampling on the same schedule.

Quantify at least CO and H2 for all groups with the same analytical workflow; if feasible, pair gas analysis with a targeted spectroscopic window chosen in a pilot for donor-sensitive changes under CO2.
Repeat the key TEA, TEOA, and no-amine groups sufficiently to check whether any donor-specific signature and product trend is reproducible rather than a single-run artifact.
measurements: Gas-phase CO and H2 from each group; if 13CO2 is used, isotopic composition of CO when detectable.
Operando or near-operando IR, Raman, UV-Vis, XAS, or other validated speciation signal selected by pilot for sensitivity to donor-dependent CO2-associated or catalyst-associated changes.
Pre-illumination versus illuminated spectra under matched backgrounds to distinguish pre-equilibrated adduct formation from light-dependent changes.
Medium covariates needed for comparability, such as pH or other donor-induced bulk changes, noting that these covariates do not establish identical local chemistry.

If a donor-specific spectroscopic feature appears, its presence or absence across groups; the signal can indicate association or state change but cannot alone prove a complete catalytic pathway or exact structure without independent assignment support.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible CO2-associated spectroscopic feature or isotopically bounded behavior present with TEOA but absent in both TEA and no-amine groups, or substantially stronger with TEOA while upstream electron-supply observables remain similar in the matched comparison. Additional support would be TEOA-specific changes in CO/H2 output that track that signature across repeats.
candidates.refutes: Evidence would weigh against H05 if TEA and TEOA show no meaningful difference in the targeted signatures or 13CO2-bounded behavior under matched conditions, and any catalytic differences are absent or better aligned with bulk medium changes or known quenching differences rather than donor-specific CO2-associated states. A complete loss of the original TEA/TEOA selectivity difference under stricter controls would also weaken the hypothesis.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if signals are below detection, poorly assigned, not reproducible, or changed together with uncontrolled covariates such as amine-induced medium shifts. Similar product outputs with insufficient spectroscopic sensitivity, or donor-specific spectra without validated relation to catalysis, also remain non-discriminating.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, irradiation settings, or acquisition windows. Use the reported P01 formulation where explicitly supplied; otherwise verify from source records or run a pilot that first identifies a stable baseline with detectable CO and H2 and a measurable donor-sensitive spectral region. For TEA substitution, start with the same nominal donor role used in the baseline and document any bulk-property mismatch. If signal saturation or no signal occurs, adjust only the analytical acquisition settings or sample path length before changing chemistry. Use 13CO2 only after natural-abundance runs show sufficient CO signal for isotopic discrimination.
candidates.limitations: TEA and TEOA differ simultaneously in donor, base, coordination, and medium effects, so even a single-factor formulation change does not isolate one microscopic cause. Cross-system literature on Re or other catalysts motivates but does not prove analogous Co-bpy adducts. No-amine controls may strongly suppress catalysis, limiting comparison to necessity rather than selectivity. Spectroscopic assignments may be ambiguous without orthogonal confirmation, and recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state.

candidates.title: Cobalt-linked adduct screen
candidates.purpose: Screen whether TEA versus TEOA under matched P01 conditions gives donor-specific CO2-derived or substrate-associated operando signals that are cobalt-dependent, while limiting inference to descriptive cobalt-linked differences unless assignment controls succeed.
candidates.source_to_proposal: GX011 motivates a transferable possibility that TEOA can participate in catalyst-associated adduct chemistry, but only in a Re system. EV004 and EV068 support operando state-sensitive measurements to separate catalyst-state changes from intermediate-related signals. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and altered active species can mimic catalyst-linked behavior, so no-cobalt and dark references are necessary. EV080 and GX008 support adding isotopic/orthogonal assignment controls rather than relying on a single spectral feature. This proposal transfers control logic and measurement strategy, not a proven Co mechanism.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor comparison. If substrate-associated observables differ while cobalt-sensitive observables remain similar, that supports donor-specific substrate/intermediate chemistry without requiring a distinct cobalt state. If cobalt-sensitive observables also differ, donor effects may include cobalt coordination or speciation changes.
Tests whether TEOA-associated features require cobalt. A feature seen only with cobalt supports a catalyst-linked interpretation but does not by itself prove a discrete cobalt-CO2 adduct.
TEA analogue of the cobalt-dependence test. Comparison with the TEOA pair helps judge whether cobalt dependence is donor-specific or a general background effect.
Tests whether observed TEOA features are operating-state light-dependent signals or dark pre-equilibrium species. This is not a donor-identity test.
Assignment control. A reproducible isotope-sensitive shift in a donor-specific feature supports CO2-derived character; absence of a shift weakens a CO2-derived assignment for that feature.

procedure: Prepare source-verified matched P01 samples and controls, varying only the listed factors and documenting reactor, gas handling, and optical cell geometry.
Run a pilot to choose observable windows and acquisition settings that give reproducible donor-to-donor baselines above solvent and g-C3N4 background; drop methods that fail this check.
Collect during-reaction cobalt-sensitive and IR measurements for all groups, with matched backgrounds; add EPR only if the pilot shows resolvable signals under the same sampling configuration.
Use the isotopic group only to test assignment of selected donor-specific bands or features; require agreement with cobalt-dependence or light-dependence before calling a feature catalyst-linked.
Report bounded conclusions separately for cobalt dependence, light dependence, and isotope sensitivity; do not infer a unique intermediate identity from one method alone.
measurements: Operando cobalt-sensitive observables indicating donor-correlated changes in cobalt oxidation state or coordination environment; useful for state comparison but not sufficient alone to assign an intermediate.

Operando IR features in regions plausibly associated with CO2-derived, carbonate-like, bicarbonate-like, or metal-associated species, interpreted only against matched no-cobalt, dark, and isotope controls.
If pilot-feasible, operando EPR signals tracking paramagnetic cobalt or radical populations; useful for donor-dependent electronic-state differences but not for full structural assignment.
Feature persistence or loss in no-cobalt and dark controls, and isotope-sensitive shifts in selected features, to distinguish catalyst-linked and CO2-derived behavior from donor/background bands.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA/TEOA difference in operando substrate-associated observables under matched conditions, where the key feature is cobalt-dependent and/or tracks donor-specific cobalt-state change, and at least one donor-specific feature also shows isotope behavior consistent with CO2-derived origin.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be no reproducible donor-specific operando difference after matched controls, or donor-specific signals fully reproduced without cobalt and lacking isotope support or cobalt-state correlation, making cobalt-linked substrate-adduct chemistry unnecessary.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include unresolved overlap, donor-dependent background absorption, absent cobalt-sensitive resolution, or isotope tests that fail because the relevant feature is too weak. Such outcomes can still justify descriptive reporting of similarities or differences without mechanistic assignment.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not assume spectral windows, concentrations, or irradiation settings from unrelated systems. Use source-verified P01 settings if available; otherwise pilot identical cell geometry, gas flow, and background subtraction across all groups. Advance a method only if donor comparisons can be collected under the same sampling configuration and with reproducible baseline correction.
candidates.limitations: Direct Co-bpy evidence for TEA/TEOA adduct chemistry is absent in the supplied record. Heterogeneous background from g-C3N4 and mixed media may obscure weak bands. Isotope sensitivity supports CO2-derived character but may not distinguish amine-linked from cobalt-linked structures. No-cobalt controls change the coordination environment and therefore support but do not prove catalyst-linked assignment.

evidence.role: direct evidence that TEOA can participate non-innocently yet CO can still derive from CO2
evidence.claim: A 2023 homogeneous photochemical study investigated TEOA impacts and reported CO formation in aqueous TEOA solution without other additives under light irradiation, while isotope labeling confirmed the CO product originated from CO2 rather than TEOA decomposition.
evidence.transfer_limit: Catalyst/system identity is not given in this snippet and differs from the Co(II)-bipyridine comparison. It does not compare TEA versus TEOA, but it directly motivates origin controls and consideration of TEOA decomposition-coupled chemistry.
evidence.reason: This is a reported observation with an origin control. It is relevant because TEOA-specific chemistry could confound interpretation of donor effects, yet the isotope result bounds one alternative explanation.

evidence.claim: In a photocatalytic CO2 reduction system, increasing TEOA proportion increased CO evolution to an optimum; the source attributes this to sacrificial quenching/electron transfer requirements and to amine-CO2 interaction that can increase dissolved CO2 through ion-pair formation.
evidence.transfer_limit: This evidence concerns variation of TEOA concentration, not a TEA-versus-TEOA comparison, and arises from a COF-Co material rather than the researcher's Co(II)-bipyridine complex. The mechanistic explanations are author interpretations rather than directly isolated proof.
evidence.reason: Useful for generating competing explanations for donor-dependent product distributions: donor effects may arise from reductive quenching kinetics, proton-transfer behavior, or CO2 capture/solvation chemistry rather than intrinsic cobalt-site changes. It is transferable as hypothesis support with explicit system and interpretation limits.

It informs controllable formulation variables more than the specific TEA/TEOA cause.
evidence.reason: Relevant because it explicitly uses CoCl2 and bipyridine in photocatalytic CO2 reduction with CO/H2 as outputs and demonstrates that product distribution is sensitive to medium composition. This strengthens the need for strict comparability controls when testing TEA versus TEOA in related systems.

evidence.reason: Relevant because it directly raises two competing explanations highly pertinent to the target question: donor-derived products and in situ formation of a different active species. decisions.rationale: This is a defensible descriptive characterization candidate for H05 because it directly tests the hypothesis prediction that TEA versus TEOA can change CO2-associated speciation under matched P01 conditions before illumination. The proposal appropriately limits inference: it does not claim catalytic relevance or exact structure, and it includes CO2 versus inert and no-amine controls to bound background donor and gas effects. Support from the supplied record is transferred rather than direct, mainly from cross-system TEOA adduct/speciation observations and method logic for assignment controls, but the transfer is used conservatively. The main comparison is well aligned to the stated question, and the candidate remains valuable even if results are only descriptive.

major_issues: No TEA-side isotope controls are included, so CO2-derived or H-involving assignment is bounded mainly for TEOA and not symmetrically for the TEA versus TEOA comparison.
The cobalt-absent control is only specified for TEOA, leaving donor-specific background separation incomplete for TEA.
The proposal mixes donor comparison with assignment logic but does not fully ensure that any donor-difference claim is equally well bounded in both donor conditions.
decisions.rationale: This candidate has clear scientific value because operando IR with isotope controls is a strong way to test whether TEA and TEOA produce different reaction-state signatures in P01. The supplied evidence supports the control logic well at the methodological level, and the candidate explicitly avoids overclaiming unique structures or pathways. However, the current design bounds assignments asymmetrically: 13CO2, D2O, and cobalt-absent controls are centered on TEOA, while the central hypothesis requires comparing TEA and TEOA. That does not invalidate the screen, but it weakens the inferential strength of a donor-specific conclusion. Revision should add symmetric TEA-side assignment or background controls, or narrow the claim to a TEOA-focused descriptive assignment study plus a less strongly assigned TEA comparison.

This is a defensible candidate because it asks a narrower, well-bounded question: whether any TEA/TEOA product difference in P01 survives when CO is explicitly confirmed as CO2-derived and donor-dependent background gas formation is checked. The design includes matched 13CO2 donor substitution plus inert-gas and dark controls, and the card correctly limits interpretation by noting that isotopic product origin does not identify adducts or cobalt states. Evidence support is partly direct for the value of CO2-origin controls and partly transferable for medium sensitivity and donor-confounding concerns. The dark control is explicitly recognized as descriptive if only one donor is selected, which is an appropriate limitation rather than a fatal flaw.

major_issues: The proposal depends on a quenching assay and an adduct-sensitive spectral method that are not actually established within the supplied P01 evidence, so the central discriminator may not yet be implementation-ready.

The inference target is strong—showing donor-specific downstream chemistry despite similar quenching observables—but similarity thresholds and comparability criteria for quenching are left undefined and pilot-dependent.

Without explicit negative controls such as no-cobalt, inert-gas, or dark references in the core group set, donor-dependent spectral differences may remain hard to assign against background or bulk-medium changes.
decisions.rationale: This is conceptually valuable because it tries to discriminate H05 from the competing pure-quenching explanation by integrating quenching observables with donor-dependent spectroscopy. The supplied evidence supports the competing-quenching rationale and gives transferable support for donor-linked adduct/speciation possibilities. However, compared with E25 and E26, this card assumes more unproven infrastructure: a usable P01 quenching assay and a validated adduct-sensitive spectroscopic readout. It also asks for stronger causal interpretation than the present control structure fully supports. Revision should either narrow the claim to an integrated exploratory correlation study or add clearer control logic and pre-specified comparability criteria for quenching versus downstream signals.

This is a useful and appropriately bounded discrimination test. It asks whether donor presence is necessary for any CO2-associated signature and whether TEOA shows something beyond a generic amine effect, using TEA, TEOA, and no-amine matched P01 groups plus optional 13CO2 bounding. The design does not pretend that TEA and TEOA are chemically equivalent aside from concentration, and it explicitly records bulk covariates instead of assuming equality. The candidate remains descriptive if assignments are partial, but that is acceptable for shortlist status because the stated conclusions are limited and the controls are relevant to H05.

major_issues: Signal assignment risk is high because the candidate combines multiple observables and possible species classes, yet no isotopic control is included in the core design to help distinguish CO2-derived substrate-associated features from donor/background bands.

The proposal seeks to relate donor-specific substrate-associated signals to cobalt-state or coordination changes, but the paired spectroscopy package is left too open-ended for strong inference at the current stage.

No-cobalt controls help, but absence in no-cobalt samples would still not cleanly prove catalyst-linked adducts; the candidate acknowledges this, so the remaining issue is that the intended conclusion may outrun the specified controls unless narrowed.
decisions.rationale: This candidate has value as a specialist screen because it explicitly tries to separate cobalt-linked effects from bulk donor/CO2 chemistry and includes TEA/TEOA plus no-cobalt and dark references. The methodological support from the supplied evidence is mainly transferable and suitable for proposing operando state-sensitive work. However, the current version risks overbroad interpretation from complex, potentially overlapping spectroscopies without sufficiently bounded assignment logic. A revision that narrows the goal to descriptive cobalt-dependence screening, or that adds isotope or orthogonal assignment controls, would improve inferential strength without needing to reject the concept.

previous_review.overall: Using only the supplied record, all six candidates are scientifically plausible transfer tests for H05 rather than directly evidenced Co-bpy results. E25, E27, and E29 are the strongest shortlist options because their questions are narrower, their controls are better matched to the stated inferences, and they keep conclusions descriptive where assignment certainty is limited. E26, E28, and E30 should be retained but revised because their intended mechanistic discrimination presently exceeds their symmetric controls, assignment-bounding strategy, or implementation specificity. None of the candidates warrants rejection on feasibility alone, but the review should preserve caution that TEA versus TEOA is a bundled chemical substitution, not a single microscopic variable, and that product or spectral differences alone do not prove catalyst-linked adduct formation.
